exact_theorem: Let T_Z be the canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) supplied by a verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum, and take as given the support filtration of a verified C66-SUPPORT-FILTRATION result: an admissible chain for Y, and a finite filtration of T_Z by sub-Hodge structures whose graded pieces are indexed by the stratum dimensions n of that chain, each a subquotient of W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q)(n), zero for n <= 7 and for n >= 17, a finite direct sum of Q(8) for n = 8, and at most one per dimension, so that at most eight pieces remain, at most one for each n with 9 <= n <= 16. Prove T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). By the verified implication of that filtration it is sufficient to fix one admissible chain and prove, for each of its strata of dimension n with 9 <= n <= 16, that the corresponding graded piece is a finite direct sum of Q(8), for instance by determining W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) or by proving that the graded piece vanishes; any other complete proof of the displayed conclusion is equally admissible. A disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface; non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof, and neither is a non-Tate group W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) unless the corresponding graded piece of the verified filtration is itself proved non-Tate. This theorem does not itself assemble the complementary target terms.
route_policy: A blocked route may appear in methods_used only when new_inputs contains a matching route and evidence description.
